And prone about me  I see them, hushed and sleeping in the hut,  Made solemn and holy by the night,  In the dead light o' the moon:  Shadowy, swathed in their blankets,  As sleep, in hewn sepulchral caves,  Egypt's and Asia's kings. arxiv-2106-06383.title: Local and Global Existence for Non-local Multi-Species Advection-Diffusion Models Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE .
arxiv-2106-06383.creator: Valeria Giunta, Thomas Hillen, Mark A. Lewis, Jonathan R. Potts
arxiv-2106-06383.description: Abstract Non-local advection is a key process in a range of biological systems, from cells within individuals to the movement of whole organisms. Consequently, in recent years, there has been increasing attention on modelling non-local advection mathematically. These often take the form of partial differential equations, with integral terms modelling the non-locality.

arxiv-2202-12213.description: Abstract Geodesics are the shortest curves between any two points on a given surface. Geodesics in the state space of quantum systems play an important role in the theory of geometric phases, as these are also the curves along which the acquired geometric phase is zero.

arxiv-2206-06546.title: Individual addressing of trapped ion qubits with geometric phase gates
arxiv-2206-06546.creator: R. T. Sutherland, R. Srinivas, D. T. C. Allcock
arxiv-2206-06546.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by R. T. Sutherland, R. Srinivas, D. T. C. Allcock. We propose a new scheme for individual addressing of trapped ion qubits, selecting them via their motional frequency. We show that geometric phase gates can perform single-qubit rotations using the coherent interference of spin-independent and (global) spin-dependent forces. The spin-independent forces, which can be generated via localised electric fields, increase the gate speed while reducing its sensitivity to motional decoherence, which we show analytically and numerically.

arxiv-2306-01348.title: Reducing Popularity Bias in Recommender Systems through AUC-Optimal Negative Sampling
arxiv-2306-01348.creator: Bin Liu, Eerjia Chen, Bang Wang*
arxiv-2306-01348.description: Abstract Popularity bias is a persistent issue associated with recommendation systems, posing challenges to both fairness and efficiency. Existing literature widely acknowledges that reducing popularity bias often requires sacrificing recommendation accuracy. In this paper, we challenge this commonly held belief.

arxiv-2312-03367.title: Lazy- k k : Decoding for Constrained Information Extraction
arxiv-2312-03367.creator: Arthur Hemmer, Mickaël Coustaty, Nicola Bartolo, Jérôme Brachat, Jean-Marc Ogier
arxiv-2312-03367.description: Abstract We explore the possibility of improving probabilistic models in structured prediction. Specifically, we combine the models with constrained decoding approaches in the context of token classification for information extraction. The decoding methods search for constraint-satisfying label-assignments while maximizing the total probability.

arxiv-2409-15600.creator: Rahul Khorana rahul.khorana@berkeley.edu, Marcus Noack marcusnoack@lbl.gov, Jin Qian jqian2@lbl.gov

A representation of a molecule or material should be invariant to the symmetries of physics, unique, continuous, efficient and general ( Langer et al., 2022 ) . These properties, however, are hard to satisfy at once: a descriptor invariant under the full orthogonal group O ⁡ ( 3 ) \Orth(3) gives a molecule and its mirror image the same value, and so cannot distinguish enantiomers whose properties differ.

arxiv-2503-17353.title: NdLinear: Don’t Flatten! Building Superior Neural Architectures by Preserving N-D Structure
arxiv-2503-17353.creator: Alex Reneau, Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu, Zhongfang Zhuang, Ting-Chun Liu, Xiang He, Judah Goldfeder, Nadav Timor, Allen G Roush, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv
arxiv-2503-17353.description: Abstract Many high-impact machine learning tasks involve multi-dimensional data such as images, volumetric medical scans, and multivariate time-series. Yet, most neural architectures flatten these inputs, discarding critical cross-dimension information. We introduce NdLinear , a novel linear transformation that circumvents this destructive flattening by operating directly on tensors.

arxiv-2505-07202.title: On the Cost and Benefits of Training Context with Utterance or Full Conversation Training: A Comparative Study
arxiv-2505-07202.creator: Hyouin Liu, Zhikuan Zhang
arxiv-2505-07202.description: Abstract Modern TTS systems designed for conversations achieve high-quality utterances but often remain inaccessible publicly. Are existing open-source architectures inadequate, or are current training techniques insufficient? This paper investigates prominent models and their underlying behaviors regarding conversational context. Using 20 GPU-hours on an NVIDIA H100, we empirically examine two approaches: context-based utterance-level training versus full conversation training.

arxiv-2507-00450.title: Shell effects in quasi-fission for calcium induced reactions forming thorium isotopes
arxiv-2507-00450.creator: C. Simenel, A.S. Umar, K. Godbey, P. McGlynn
arxiv-2507-00450.description: Abstract Quantum shell effects induce an asymmetric fission mode in actinides, which disappears in neutron deficient isotopes. Quasi-fission, characterized by a significant mass transfer in heavy ion collisions at low-energies, is expected to be affected by similar shell effects. This is studied in 40-56 Ca + 176 +^{176} Yb reactions with the time-dependent Hartree-Fock approach.

Angeles Juanes
pmc-12534982.description: Human dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) is the rate-limiting enzyme in pyrimidine de novo synthesis and represents a promising target for cancer therapy. However, current inhibitors of DHODH have limited clinical effectiveness and adverse effects. Herein, we report NK-A 17E-233I, a novel small-molecule inhibitor of the human DHODH enzyme, identified through a prospective virtual screening methodology.
